own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = E (1 - exp(-t/RC)), tau = 0.1 s

defect_reasons.other: Wording only: 'broken again' (T3BCA, T8648) implies an earlier break that never happened, and 'cut off from the battery' (TE931, T3ED2) relies on the reader inferring that no discharge path remains for the capacitor.

notes: All certified answers verified: base 12(1 - e^-0.8) = 6.60805 V; extra 1.5/3.5/7 kOhm give tau = 0.13/0.17/0.24 s and 5.5148/4.50438/3.40162 V; break at 30/60 ms gives 12(1 - e^-0.3) = 3.11018 V and 12(1 - e^-0.6) = 5.41426 V; K values 250/400/750 ms all exceed 80 ms, so 6.60805 V. Minimal pairs hold: T61C2/T0ED4 both 3.5 kOhm, differ only in 'taken out again' vs 'left there'; T68E7/TE7F1 both 3.5 kOhm, differ only in attachment (separate loop vs charging loop). The 60 ms R sentences are linked to the 400 ms K sentences by outside_regime_of, not claimed minimal pairs, so the different number is intended. Numeral-free twins TC38C and T4C87 match their twins. The non-leaking-capacitor assumption needed for the out-of-regime R answers is listed. Change from pass 1: on reflection, cutting a series R-C branch off from the battery leaves the capacitor with no closed loop, so the open-circuit reading is the physical one and I lower that wording concern from medium to low and rate clarity clear; pass 1 is unchanged.
